_meta.description: Star Rupture power-supply, base-core and amplifier reference. Used by the partitioning + power-sizing pass to choose the cheapest generator mix per base and to decide when to upgrade a base core vs. add an amplifier.
sources: data/buildings_and_recipes.json (canonical for power/heat/coreHeatCapacity values used by the existing GraphML)
Steam Community guide 'StarRupture Base Core Upgrade Guide' (id 3642402585)
Star Rupture wiki (starrupture.wiki.gg) and starruptureplanner.com guides for build costs and unlock levels
data_notes: Generator power/heat numbers come from data/buildings_and_recipes.json — they are what the existing GraphML uses for each producer/consumer node, so the bookkeeping stays internally consistent.

Several public guides quote different generator outputs (e.g. wiki lists Wind v.2 as '2,000 MW'); these are not reconciled here. If the in-game values differ, edit this file and regenerate the GraphML.
Base Core Amplifier v.1 heatCapacity is 20 per the source data; some web guides quote +50. Source data wins for the partitioning algorithm.
Power is a per-base resource — Star Rupture's 'conductive footprint' system means power does NOT cross base boundaries. The partitioning algorithm sizes generators per base accordingly.

base_core.name: Base Core
notes: heat_capacity is the cap on summed heat values for all buildings, depots, generators, dispatchers, and receivers placed in this base.
Upgrade costs for levels 1-3 not yet captured; level 4 is sourced from public upgrade guide.
Exceeding capacity drops Fire Wave protection — the base goes offline longer after each rupture. Treat the cap as hard for planning purposes.

amplifiers.name: Base Core Amplifier v.1
amplifiers.notes: Web guides quote +50 capacity; source data says +20. Source data is canonical for this codebase.

generators.name: Solar Generator v.1
generators.notes: Baseline generator. Tiny but free of fuel.

generators.name: Solar Generator v.2
generators.notes: Source data: 140 kW. Wiki quotes 1000 — treat with skepticism until verified in-game.

generators.name: Wind Turbine v.1
generators.notes: Source data: 1200 kW. Wiki/guides quote 200 — discrepancy unresolved.

generators.name: Wind Turbine v.2
generators.notes: Source data: 3200 kW. Wiki quotes 2000 — discrepancy unresolved.

generators.name: Chemical Generator
notes: Source data: 8200 kW power, 400 heat. Some web guides quote much smaller numbers.
Consumes fuel (presumed basicfuel) but consumption rate not yet captured.
Highest heat per generator — eats a lot of base capacity.
generator_selection_order is a default preference list for picking generators per base: try larger/cheaper-per-kW first, fall back as unlock prerequisites or heat budget fail.

The partitioning algorithm should pack production buildings into bases first (respecting heat caps), then size generators for each base's summed kW demand, then re-check that generators themselves fit in the remaining heat budget. If a base's generators bust the budget, either upgrade the base level, add amplifiers, or split the base.
Power across base boundaries is not supported in-game — each base needs its own generator mix. Cross-base item movement uses Cargo Dispatcher → Cargo Receiver pairs (see data/transport.json).
